title: South America surge readiness brief — dry run schedule and ops checklist
content:
Objective:
Run a targeted dry run to validate South America (sa) region GPU surge handling, verify failover routing to US-West/US-East within latency budget, and exercise oncall runbook edits required for preemption-heavy spikes. This doc is the brief for the operations dry run on 2026-10-09; notes from planning and pre-checks below.

Context and motivation:
- Usage growth in LATAM has increased 3x over the last 12 weeks for a mixture of hosted API customers and a pilot dedicated tenant. We need to validate that our regional capacity + overflow routing works end-to-end without customer-visible errors under a synthetic 2x sustained QPS surge.
- Recent preemption experiments showed KV cache warming regressions when multi-region failover happened; this drill explicitly includes KV prefix-warm and degraded-cache scenarios.

Attendees (planning):
- Miguel Torres (owner) — infra capacity lead
- Priya Nair — SRE lead (monitoring, alerts)
- Ethan Park — serving runtime engineer (batching/caching)
- Zara Patel — network & peering lead
- Lucas Gomez — oncall rotation coordinator (LATAM)
- Guest: Ana Ruiz — product (customer impact evaluation)

High-level success criteria (pass/fail):
1) No 5xx rate increase above 0.5% during surge window for hosted public API routes (measured per-minute).
2) P95 end-to-end latency for routed calls to fallback region remains <= 450ms for short completions (<128 tokens).
3) Rolling failover and fallback completes under 6 minutes for simulated regional outage signal.
4) KV prefix warm fallback reduces token marginal latency impact by at least 20% vs cold fallback (measured after simulated failover).
5) All oncall runbook steps execute without manual escalation beyond the primary responder.

Planned load & capacity assumptions:
- Baseline sa-region serving capacity: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed nodes). Typical utilization: 62% 3pm local.
- Synthetic surge: gradually ramp to 2x baseline QPS over 10 minutes and hold for 30 minutes, then step to 3x for 10 minutes to validate overcommit/fallback paths.
- Expected spill policy: route overflow to US-West until US-West saturation threshold of 70% GPU queue depth, then cascade to US-East.
- Latency budget used for decisioning: 500ms soft, 750ms hard on client-facing SLAs.

Dry-run schedule (2026-10-09, all times BRT / America/Sao_Paulo):
- 09:00 — Pre-checks: dashboards up, dashboards pinned in #infra-south-america, telemetry ingestion sanity check, RBAC keys confirmed, and alert thresholds verified by Priya.
- 09:30 — Canary load: 0.5x baseline for 10 minutes to validate traffic generator config. Observe APM, tail latency.
- 09:45 — Ramp to 2x over 10 minutes. Primary responder (Lucas) watches oncall feed; Ethan watches batch queues and KV hit rates.
- 10:05 — Hold 2x for 30 minutes. During hold: run synthetic KV-warm tests by issuing prefix-heavy requests with structured prompts.
- 10:35 — Step to 3x for 10 minutes to force overflow routing. Verify routing decisions and model variant fallbacks.
- 10:50 — Simulated control-plane regional outage (manual failover trigger via runbook). Validate rollbacks and traffic drain procedures.
- 11:05 — Recovery window: restore regional control-plane; exercise cache re-warm steps and observe model quality/regression metrics.
- 11:30 — Retrospective: capture metrics, incident timeline, runbook gaps, action items.

Monitoring checklist (pre-run):
- Dashboards: SA-region capacity heatmap, token-level cost stream, queue-depth per instance, request routing map, model variant fallback counts.
- Alerts: surge-latency-p95, gpu-queue-depth-high, fallback-to-us-west, kv-cache-hit-drop.
- Synthetic tests: health-check endpoints for model-serving, small-completion RTT test, ephemeral-key access test to KMS.

Test scenarios to exercise in-run:
- Cold-cache failover: annotate traces for first-request KV miss pattern for a 256-token completion after failover.
- Partial preemption: simulate preemptible node reclaim and ensure autoscaler drains & rebalances without erroneous 503s.
- Peering degradation: throttle inter-region egress by 30% to emulate network contention; observe TTL-based route decisions.
- Model variant fallback: force high-latency on full-precision models to ensure policy routes to quantized variant and preserves output shape.

Runbook changes to validate (short summary):
- Add step 2.3: "Confirm KV warming job queued (sa-kv-rewarm) before external traffic ramp beyond 1.5x".
- Update alert thresholds: reduce fallback-to-us-west flapping suppression window from 5m to 3m.
- New play: "peering-slowdown": temporary route preferences and NACK-handling for long-tail requests (>2000ms).

Risks & mitigations identified during planning:
- Risk: Synthetic load may trigger customer alerting if not properly labelled. Mitigation: use test tenancy and annotated auth tokens; product (Ana) to pre-notify any pilot customers.
- Risk: KV rewarm job competes with production reclaim for GPU memory leading to OOM. Mitigation: cap rewarm concurrency to 10% of region GPUs and prioritize low-memory model variants.
- Risk: Rollout automation bug causes mismatch in model versions between regions. Mitigation: take a config snapshot and do a dry-config-apply validation step; fallback to snapshot if mismatch detected.

Decision points (pre-run):
- Use test tenant (redwood-surge-test) for all synthetic traffic — agreed.
- Autoscaler borrow policy will allow 4 nodes of dedicated capacity to be borrowed from staging pools during the run; staging owners signed off.
- Post-run plan: retention of telemetry snapshots for 30 days in the infra-eval bucket for faster analysis.

Post-run measurement plan:
- Primary graphs to export: per-route 5xx rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, spill ratio to US-West/US-East, KV hit rate delta pre/post failover, GPU CPU & memory distribution during peak.
- Cost telemetry: estimate incremental token cost of spill to US regions and report delta per 10k requests.
- Quality: run a 200-prompt regression eval against pre-failover baseline to check for model output drift due to variant fallback.

Action items (owners & target dates):
- Miguel: finalize dry-run script and post the pinned agenda to #infra-south-america by 2026-10-07 EOD.
- Priya: create and validate alert mute schedule & PagerDuty overrides; due 2026-10-08 12:00.
- Ethan: implement KV rewarm cap and add instrumentation for rewarm job; due 2026-10-08 18:00.
- Zara: coordinate peering throttle knobs in staging peering fabric and prepare failback plan; due 2026-10-08 17:00.
- Lucas: update oncall schedule for 2026-10-09 and confirm primary/secondary responders; due 2026-10-07 14:00.
- Ana: notify affected pilot customers and draft customer-facing post-mortem template; due 2026-10-08 16:00.

Notes and loose thoughts (working):
- If we see consistent p95 > 600ms on spill, experiment with selective early-return (partial-completion) for low-value requests as emergency throttle.
- Consider a short-lived regional quota burst permission for strategic customers to avoid silent failures during scheduled maintenance windows.
- Follow-up spike: investigate whether prefix-aware caching (split by tenant namespace) yields better warm-up in failover than global prefix rewarm.

Appendix (quick commands / links):
- Trigger failover (runbook step): /bin/runbook trigger-region-failover --region sa --mode simulated
- KV rewarm orchestration job: ops/jobs/sa-kv-rewarm (k8s cronjob)
- Dashboards: grafana/redwood/sa-capacity-heatmap, datadog/infra/sa-routing
- Post-run retrospective doc: to be created as shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/retrospectives/sa-surge-dryrun-2026-10-09

End of brief.
